item.research_question: How can massive amounts of interstitial elements (O, C, N) be dissolved in a metallic host lattice without forming brittle ceramic phases, while simultaneously achieving near-theoretical strength and large deformability?
item.material_system: TiNbZr-O-C-N massive interstitial solid solution (MISS) alloys, specifically (TiNbZr)86O12C1N1 (at%) referred to as O-12 MISS alloy, and reference alloys (TiNbZr)92O6C1N1 (O-6), (TiNbZr)92O8 (O-8), and equiatomic TiNbZr
item.processing_route: Magnetron sputtering on Si (001) substrates with Ar pressure of 0.3 Pa and substrate bias power of 90 W, followed by annealing in a vacuum (10−2 Pa) at 500 °C for 2 h to promote interstitial diffusion
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial compression of micropillars (diameter 1.0–1.6 μm) at ambient temperature with a nominal strain rate of 5 × 10−3 s−1; in-situ SEM bending and tensile tests at ambient temperature
key_findings: The O-12 MISS alloy contains 12 at% interstitial O with no oxides, carbides, or nitrides formed.
The alloy exhibits an ultrahigh compressive yield strength of 4.2 ± 0.2 GPa.
The alloy maintains large deformability of 65% strain at ambient temperature without localized shear deformation.
The shear stress ratio τy/G reaches 1/18, approaching the theoretical limit of ~1/10.
In bending tests, the O-12 alloy shows an ultrahigh flow stress of 5.6 ± 0.5 GPa and withstands a tensile strain of 54%.
Grain refinement occurs during deformation, reducing grain diameters from 20–50 nm to 5–20 nm at ~65% strain.
C and N segregate to grain boundaries with concentrations of 1.8 ± 0.3 at% and 1.0 ± 0.2 at%, respectively.
The elastic modulus (E) of the O-12 alloy is 95 GPa, while the shear modulus (G) is calculated to be 38 GPa.
item.mechanism: Massive interstitial O atoms create strong, asymmetrical lattice distortions that impede dislocation nucleation and motion, while C and N segregation to grain boundaries reduces interfacial energy, stabilizing the boundaries against coarsening and suppressing localized shear deformation; this combination promotes dislocation multiplication and grain refinement without softening.
item.limitations: The study notes that thermodynamic calculations cannot fully consider lattice distortions and interstitial site variations in concentrated solid solutions, and that Ga+ ion beam milling could potentially alter surface layers, though this was minimized.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the MISS alloy design strategy is applicable to a wide range of materials including alloys with multiple principal elements and may provide fundamental insights into plastic deformation in massive interstitially doped solid solutions.
quotes: Here we introduce a class of massive interstitial solid solution (MISS) alloys by using a highly distorted substitutional host lattice, which enables solution of massive amounts of interstitials as an additional principal element class, without forming ceramic phases.

The alloy reveals an ultrahigh compressive yield strength of 4.2 GPa, approaching the theoretical limit, and large deformability (65% strain) at ambient temperature, without localized shear deformation.
The O interstitials promote dislocation multiplication at high stress levels, while the C and N segregation to grain boundaries suppresses the localized deformation.
